key_insight: A GPT-4-guided decision tree built from the 2017 McDonald criteria could identify multiple sclerosis from first neurology notes with fairly strong accuracy and interpretable step-by-step reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLMs may help triage and standardize early MS case detection from clinical documentation, but they should support—not replace—clinician review.
method: 125 first neurology notes from a clinic cohort (MS, related disorders, and controls) were analyzed.
Assessment/plan sections were redacted; only history and diagnostic testing text was used.
GPT-4 made binary decisions at each decision-tree node using expert-curated MS knowledge based on the 2017 McDonald criteria.
evidence_signal: Against neurologist-assessed diagnoses, the system achieved 84% accuracy, 79% precision, 74% recall, and 91% specificity, with hallucinations noted in 26% of cases.
watch_item: Hallucinations and reasoning errors still led to misclassifications, so external validation and safeguards are needed before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Large Language Model - Enhanced Decision Tree Framework for Identifying Multiple Sclerosis Diagnoses from Clinical Documentation
